🎃 Good Thursday afternoon — and welcome to October! Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 626 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Hot new space experiments
 
Illustration: Natalie Peeples/Axios

Several futuristic space experiments launched into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket this afternoon, Alex Fitzpatrick reports.

🚀 Among the 130 payloads aboard the Transporter-18 "rideshare" mission:

  1. Google's MVP satellite, designed to test the concept of solar-powered data centers in space. (N.Y. Times gift link)
  2. Protostar, a satellite from startup Star Catcher meant to transmit energy to another satellite — to bear out the idea of an orbital power grid. (Go deeper.)
  3. Reason-1, a satellite from startup Cowboy Space designed to collect solar energy in space and beam it to Earth.

🔌 Cowboy Space founder and CEO Baiju Bhatt tells Axios that the idea is to provide power in places without an existing power grid — a kind of Starlink for energy — while also working toward orbital data centers.

  • There are also potential military applications, Bhatt adds — powering high-endurance surveillance drones, for example.

🤔 Reality check: It's early days for all of these concepts, which have long existed on drawing boards and in sci-fi novels but have yet to be borne out.

The big picture: It's a boom time for intriguing commercial efforts in Earth orbit, though SpaceX's plan to wind down its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket has left the space industry scrambling for launch alternatives.

2. 📰 WSJ: DOJ reviewing Nixon treatment
 
Former President Nixon salutes during a 1968 campaign stop in El Paso. Photo: Bettmann/CORBIS/Bettmann Archive

The Justice Department is "reviewing whether the special prosecutor's office that investigated the famed Watergate break-in committed misconduct," The Wall Street Journal reports.

  • That comes after former Nixon aide Geoff Shepard "recently gave a two-hour presentation" at the DOJ on "his theory that the deep state took Nixon down," per the paper.

🧑‍⚖️ The WSJ reports: "Shepard has served as a sort of godfather for the Watergate revisionists."

  • "His scholarship has unearthed a number of primary-source documents which he says show Nixon and his associates weren't treated fairly."

A DOJ spokesperson tells Axios: "Given his expertise and scholarship on Watergate, [Shepard] was recently invited to give a presentation to [the Office of Professional Responsibility], but that presentation does not constitute an investigation."

The big picture: Nixon is hot these days among some conservatives (especially "Nixonmaxxing" youth), who see parallels between his treatment and the investigations into President Trump.

4. 🫎 1 for the road: Wildlife bridge a "huge success"
 
Greenland Overpass in Colorado. Photo: Robert Sanchez/Axios

Pronghorn and elk are taking the high road in Colorado, Axios Douglas County's Robert Sanchez reports.

  • The animals are crossing I-25 on the Greenland Wildlife Overpass — a promising sign that the project is helping animals find one another for breeding opportunities, as intended.

📸 The overpass opened in December, and the first elk appeared on camera in June, officials say.

  • Pronghorn are making the trip, too — along with mule deer, black bears, mountain lions and more.

Colorado DOT environmental manager Chuck Attardo says: "Based on the video feed that we're collecting, huge success."
